correctness.rationale: The lead source gives the coefficient identities connecting a2,a3 to the first two coefficients of a positive-real-part function and the standard formulas for Gamma1,Gamma2. The exact Schur parameterization c1=2u, c2=2(u^2+(1-|u|^2)v) therefore gives the asserted disk fibers by direct algebra. Conversely every |u|<=1, |v|<=1 is realized by a Schur function, and explicit even-odd ODE constructions lift its Cayley transform to the defining Sakaguchi class. The moduli-difference extrema are exact extrema over those disks, giving -1/sqrt(6), 1/2, -1/(3 sqrt(2)), and 1/6.

value.rationale: The two Sakaguchi classes are canonical geometric-function classes, and the fresh lead paper explicitly targets the first-two inverse-logarithmic moduli difference but displays only the upper endpoint for each. The exact disk-fiber bodies solve the natural stronger classification problem for the same coefficient pair, show precisely how the two coefficients depend on one another, recover the known upper extrema, and supply sharp lower extrema and their geometry. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of isolated coefficient maxima.
